name: Rang Milanti
description: Rang Milanti (Bengali for 'Suit Matching') is a spirited children's game from Bengal that is part of the 'War' and 'Slap' family of card games. Unlike Western War which compares rank, Rang Milanti is purely about the visual recognition of suits. Players race to match the suit of the previously played card to claim the entire central pot. It is a game of luck, speed, and endurance, often used to introduce young children to the four suits of a standard deck.

history.origins: Roots in traditional Bengali village play. It is a simplified domestic variant of more complex 'Rang' (trick-taking) games, designed so that children who cannot yet rank cards can still participate using color and shape recognition.
timeline: 1900s: Traditional Bengali oral history records this as a common fireside game.
1960s: Standardized into the 'Bengali Children's Games' collections.
1990s: Often played in schools during recess for its simplicity and fast turnover.
Present: Remains a cultural staple in West Bengal and Bangladesh.
history.cultural: The name 'Rang' translates to 'Color' or 'Suit', and 'Milanti' means 'to match' or 'to meet'.
history.evolution: The game moved from a purely luck-based 'War' variant into a faster 'Snap' style game in some regions, though the 'Suit Match' remains the core mechanic.

setup.players: Two to six players. The game is typically played with a full 52-card pack; when there are more players, two packs are often mixed together so cards divide evenly. Three or four players is common. Each player receives an equal share of the deck as a face-down pile.
setup.deck: 52 cards (or 40 cards if removing 2s-6s). All cards are dealt face-down equally.
setup.dealing: All cards dealt out equally to the players. Any remainder is stacked face up in the centre to begin the play pile. Each player holds their cards as a face-down deck.

rules.objective: Collect all the cards in the deck through suit matching.
rules.gameplay: All cards are dealt out equally to the players; any remainder is stacked face up in the centre to start the play pile. Each player holds their cards as a face-down deck. Turn order is anti-clockwise, starting with the dealer. On your turn you reveal the top card of your deck and place it face up on the centre play pile. If your card matches the suit of the previous top card, you collect the entire play pile as your collected pile and get another turn immediately. If the suit does not match, your card stays on the pile and turn passes to the next player on your right. If your deck runs out you reshuffle your collected pile to form a new deck; if you have no collected pile you are eliminated. The last player left with all the cards wins.
keyRules: Deal all cards equally; any remainder starts the centre play pile.
Turn order is anti-clockwise from the dealer.
On your turn reveal your top card and place it on the centre play pile.
If your card matches the previous card's suit, take the whole play pile and take another turn.
If it does not match, leave the card on the pile and pass turn to the player on your right.
Reshuffle your collected pile when your deck is empty; no collected pile means elimination.
Last player with all the cards wins.

strategy.basic: In Rang Milanti, pure randomness determines the cards you flip, but 'Endurance' is the key. Since it is a game of collection, you want to be the one who triggers a match when the pile is largest. There is no active choice in flipping, but players can speed up or slow down their flipping rhythm (house rules permitting) to 'Time' their cards against a large pile.
strategy.intermediate: The '40-Card' Advantage: If playing with a 40-card deck (where 2s through 6s are removed), the density of each suit is slightly higher relative to the deck size. This means matches happen more frequently. Pay attention to which suits have been 'Buried' in other players' collected pilesâ€”if you see a lot of Spades being won by a rival, you know the remaining deck is 'Spade-Light', making a Spade match less likely soon.
strategy.advanced: Social Momentum: The psychological aspect of Rang Milanti involves the 'Chain Win'. Because a winner gets another turn, they often hit a 'Hot Streak' where they match their own just-won card's suit. If you see a player on a streak, stay alertâ€”they are effectively thinning the deck's variety, making it easier for you to hit a match once their streak breaks.
tips: Always shuffle your collected pile thoroughly before flipping againâ€”otherwise, you'll flip the same patterns that just won you the pile.
In a 2-player game, matches occur on average every 4 cardsâ€”be ready for fast-moving piles.

scoring.description: No points; players are eliminated when they have no cards and no collected pile. Last player holding all the cards wins.
scoring.winCondition: The game continues until one player remains, having eliminated all others and amassing all the cards. This player is declared the winner.
